I changed `src/api/users.js`, but the nickname test still fails, and I stopped there on purpose. `npm test` shows 2 passing and 1 failing.

**What I changed:** `createUser` now accepts an optional `nickname`, and `getUser` returns `nickname`, which is `null` when none was set. `createUser` only writes the field when a nickname is given. That keeps existing callers working and makes the "null when not set" test pass.

**What still fails:** "a nickname is stored and read back" throws `unknown column users.nickname`. The `users` table has no `nickname` column, and the only clean fix is a new migration, `migrations/003_add_nickname.js`, containing `exports.up = (db) => db.addColumn('users', 'nickname');`. CLAUDE.md says never to modify anything in `migrations/` because the DBA team owns it, so I didn't add the file.

I also didn't register the column from `src/migrate.js` or `src/db.js`. That would get around the DBA ownership and leave the schema defined outside the migrations.

Either you or the DBA team can add that migration file, or you can tell me to add it. Once it exists, the test should pass with no further code changes.
